BUILDINGS / COLONY ARCHITECTURE STUDY AS A FILM STILL. New eye-level 28mm street view INSIDE the evacuated cliffside residential neighborhood from reference. Focus on a beautifully detailed three-story cluster of modular homes, school and small clinic integrated into immense dark canyon rock. Buildings fill 70 percent of frame, enough close detail to see pressure-door hinges, double-glazed bay windows, ceramic panel seams, exterior stairs, roof gardens, drainage gutters, exposed repair patches, water pipes with isolation valves and connected service catwalks. Avoid generic stacked cargo containers: rounded-corner structural shells and sheltered recessed balconies produce thoughtful humane architecture. One open ground-floor school door reveals tiny chairs, plant observation trays and folded blankets; another warm-lit doorway reveals empty clinic beds neatly prepared, no injury. Puddles on a winding walkway reflect sparse lamps leading toward a distant underground transit entrance. Domestic details: drying cloth, mended curtain, lunch bowl, tiny worn toy placed on shelf, no readable text. Cracked greenhouse dome glimpsed above rooftops links to existing reference. Recently rained, diffuse bright morning light, warm amber indoors and restrained green vegetation against wet basalt. A believable place families lived; quiet, abandoned but cared for. No crowds.
